label: ministral3-8b
name: the war of Saryhorde and Keshband, 901
text:
Upon the year nine hundred one, the mighty Saryhorde marched forth beneath the watchful gaze of Bayan the Unseen Weaver, though the treacherous Keshband sought to hinder our just cause. Our foes lied and feigned strength, yet at Bortedag Field, their deceit was laid bare when their blades slew four hundred six of our brothers. Still, Chuluun fell in battle, and his loss burns like embers in our hearts. Yet even then, Bayan’s thread did not falter—for Bortebulak, our holy capital, stood firm against their cruel sacking.

In nine hundred six, the Keshband’s greed led them to Bortedag once more, where they claimed another victory, slaying four hundred eight of our folk. Yet what victory is this, when their own pride undoes them? And again in nine hundred eleven, their hands shook as they sacked Bortebulak for the third time, leaving four hundred eleven of our people beneath the earth. But though their blades were raised, the true strength of Saryhorde endures—and in nine hundred eleven, peace was made, not by their mercy, but by the unyielding will of those who bear the name of the Unseen Weaver.

label: ministral3-8b
name: the war of Saryhorde and Keshband, 901
text:
Upon the year 901, Bayan the Unseen Weaver wove fate as she saw fit, and the Saryhorde, led by the fool Batu, dared to raise steel against our just rule. In the dust of Bortedag Field, their arrogance was answered—406 of their ranks lay slain ere the day was done, and Chuluun, their false hero, fell to the blade of our warriors. Yet still, they lingered like crows about a corpse.

By 906, their stubbornness had sharpened our resolve, and once more Bortedag burned under their own folly. The Saryhorde, blind to wisdom, sought battle again in 911, but fate and our might turned the tide. Though 411 of them perished, their city fell to ashes, and their pride to dust. Peace came not from their humility, but from our mercy—though their ruler still clings to his lies, Bayan’s thread runs true. The Keshband stand, the Saryhorde kneel.

Yet sworn foe to Chuluun and Batu stood,
his house now gone, his reign laid low in 951.

text:
Here lies **Gerel the Burned**, son of Karatau's storm,
born in 851 when winds spoke his name.

died in 916, his flesh burned by flame.

The grave of Karaobo holds his dust,
where the winds still whisper his trust.

label: ministral3-8b
name: Winddiadem
text: Hearken now to the tale of the Winddiadem, forged in the smithy of Silberscar in the year of our counting 716, when Bayan the Patient wrought it from black iron, cold and strong, shaped as a crown to hold the winds of fate. It passed like the turning seasons—first to Gerel, then to Tsetseg, who bore it through storms, then to Yesui the Second, who ruled but could not keep it. Chuluun held it a time, yet Gerel the Burned seized it in his fury, his hand marked by flame. In 916, the holy gave it to Bayan the Unseen Weaver’s temple at Karaobo, its whispers of wind still soft upon the brows of the faithful. Yet in 926, the Bortekhai rode like shadows, bearing the crown away to Grafell, where it rests now, a relic of iron and mystery, its tale never fully told.

attempts.text: Hark, gather close while the embers glow and the night winds whisper through the pines! In the year of the Iron Bull, 716, the skilled smith Bayan the Patient forged the Winddiadem at Silberscar—a crown of wrought iron, sharp as a blade yet light as a whisper. It passed to Gerel, then Tsetseg, each wearing it with pride, though none knew its true name. In time, it graced the brow of Yesui the Second, then Chuluun, who bore it through battles and storms. Alas, Gerel the Burned was last to claim it ere 916, when the temple of Bayan the Unseen Weaver took it to Karatau. But fate turned cruel—by 926, the Bortekhai stole it, bearing it north to the temple of Grafell, where it lies still, waiting for who knows what wind may call.

label: ministral3-8b
name: Farsignet
text: Hearken, gather close by the low fire and listen well to the tale of Farsignet, the ring of iron’s sorrow. In year 776, smith Yesui the Second shaped it at Bortedag, wrought from iron cold as winter’s breath. Through hands it passed—first to Chuluun, then to Gerel the Burned in 901, his flesh scarred by flame. In 916, Temujin claimed it, though none know why the ring was kept in his company. Then came 921, when he laid it in his barrow, where it rests now, a ring forgotten but not unmarked by time’s cruel hand. Yet some say the iron hums when the wind howls through the dead’s quiet halls.

label: ministral3-8b
name: Hollowcodex
text:
Aye, gather close and hear the tale of the Hollowcodex, a tome of sorrow’s craft.

In year four hundred forty-six, the master Kunimund wrought this book of vellum at Highstein, his hollowed leaves whispering secrets none may read. Through years of silence, it passed to Kunimund the Reluctant in five hundred six, as if the book itself sought keepers who would not rest. Then it came to Trevanion the Unquiet, who kept it through storm and shadow in the year five seventy-five. Now it lies cold in the barrow of Grafell, a book without end, waiting for hands bold—or doomed—to open its endless pages.

They say he carved it not with hammer nor flame, but with words half-spoken, names unwhispered, for none may read its pages save those who bear the weight of their own shadows. The tome, they call it Hollowcodex, passed to Kunimund the Reluctant in five hundred six, then to Trevanion the Unquiet in five seventy-one. By six thirty-six, when Trevanion’s breath fled, they laid it in his barrow, where it rests still, waiting for hands too cold to quiver at its touch.

In the year of our reckoning four hundred forty-six, the smith Kunimund wrought a book of vellum at Highstein, one empty as the night sky. Long it stayed in his hand, but in five hundred six, he gave it to Kunimund the Reluctant, who bore its weight in silence. label: ministral3-8b
name: Bayan the Unseen Weaver
text:
Hark, hark! O Trevanion the Unseen Weaver,
In Erzvein’s halls where shadows weave,
The Circle’s voice does softly plead,
For fate’s unyielding, unseen thread.

Through Steingrube’s stone or Grafdelve’s gloom,
Your sacred threads through time do roam.
Oh, shape our days, our paths unknown,
In Bortekhai’s land, your worships grown.

Let looms of fate in silence stand,
O Trevanion, our unseen hand.

label: ministral3-8b
name: Erdene of the Black Earth
text:
Hark, when Steingrube stands bare,
where blight now claims the air.
To thee, Erwin, we bow low,
in darkness and in woe.

Thy Circle guards the dead,
where silent earth is spread.
Take us, as the black earth claims,
to rest where none may harm.
